MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  JANUARY 30, 2020

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Schmitz, Addleman, Arata, Bayer,
  Buresh, Carman, Carrese, Friedman,
  Medawar*, Seamans*, Shinn, Silvano,
  Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Stegura

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International

  * Arrived after minutes approval

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  DECEMBER 17, 2019.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
BAYER to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  DECEMBER 17, 2019.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

CHAIR SCHMITZ announced the Community Roundup on February 4, 2020, at 6:30 p.m.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  SAFETY ELEMENT

John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International (MBI), announced that Shane Burkhardt is no
longer with MBI and stated that they are looking for a candidate that would be a good fit not only
for the needs of MBI but also for the city. COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked that Mr.
Bellas relay his thank you for a good job with the city. CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked Mr. Bellas for
the consideration being given to the unique characteristics of the city.

Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, MBI, provided an overview of the types of topics which will be
covered under Natural Hazards and Man-made Hazards within the Safety Element.

CHAIR SCHMITZ, asked if pandemics are considered. Ms. Barbhaya stated that it is part of the
climate adaptation plan and related to air quality but will not go specifically into the medical
conditions unless the city chooses to include this.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  1
 MEETING MINUTES, JANUARY 30, 2020
 Ms. Barbhaya provided a presentation on specific topics of the Safety Element, which include:

  •  Seismic Earthquake Fault – The two major faults which would affect the city are the Palos
  Verdes Fault and the Cabrillo Fault.
  •  Dam Inundation Map – Flooding is not a major issue for the city.
  •  Slope Instability – Due to the topography of the city, there are areas that have the potential
  for landslides.
  •  Fire Hazard Severity Zones – The city is in a high fire hazard safety.
  •  Hazardous Material Locations
  •  Hazardous Management Overlay

John Bellas, MBI, suggested the following policy regarding street/vehicular level of service to be
added to the Safety Element:

  •  Maintain a vehicular level of service on evacuation routes that allows for emergency
  evacuation of the city in a reasonable amount of time.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR asked if the city is part of the Peninsula Emergency
Preparedness Program. Administrative Analyst Slawson stated yes, and in addition, the city is
part of the Master Mutual Aide agreements with neighboring jurisdictions.

City Manager Grammer added that if there was a need to evacuate due to a major emergency,
the Sheriff’s Department would direct the evacuation route down the hill. For example, all lanes
of Crenshaw Blvd. would go one way down the hill.

The GPAC reviewed the following policies and made the changes as noted below.

Move forward with the following changes:

    Policy 1.2 Designate Maintain and develop specific the designated critical facilities
  identified in the Local Hazardous Mitigation Plan as emergency centers to serve the entire
  City and maintain information on existing trauma care facilities that serve the region.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE, Administrative Analyst Slawson
stated that the city has partnered with the American Red Cross to pre-identify shelter locations in
the city. COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR added that the Peninsula Emergency Preparedness
program has partnered with the schools to have on-site emergency supplies and also have
volunteers who will be deployed in the case that emergency care is needed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested a policy on maintaining a list of transportation
dependent residents. Administrative Analyst Slawson stated that the city has looked into this,
however, due to HIPAA laws and the expectation that they will be prioritized, the city cannot
maintain such a list. Residents are encouraged to register with the city’s emergency alert system
to receive alerts via text or e-mail in the case of a major emergency. COMMITTEE MEMBER
MEDAWAR added that residents should also connect with their neighbors.

Move forward with the following changes:

  •  Policy 6.4 Ensure that the Los Angeles County Sanitation District implements its closure
  and reclamation plans for Palos Verdes Landfill. Coordinate with Los Angeles County
  Sanitation District to ensure that appropriate mitigation action plan and disaster response
  is in place for the Palos Verdes landfill.

Remove, already required:

  •  Policy 1.8 Require review by a structural engineer when a critical building or facility
  undergoes substantial improvements.

  •  Policy 1.9 Require site specific geotechnical analysis in areas of potential liquefaction,
  especially in and adjacent to the Chandler landfill.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  2
 MEETING MINUTES, JANUARY 30, 2020
   •  Policy 2.2 Prohibit residential development on non-engineered fill of any kind.

Remove. Enforcement is required by State Law and reported on annually:

  •  Policy 2.8 The City will continue to enforce the Water Conservation Ordinance adopted in
  1991. Not needed since the city is required by State law to enforce this ordinance and is
  required to report on this annually.

Remove, required per the Building Code:

  •  Policy 2.10 Continue to enforce a Class B Roofing Ordinance for new development but
  encourage residents with wood shingle/unrated roofing materials to retrofit or upgrade
  their roofs with resistant eaves and awnings.

Move forward with the following changes:

  • Policy 3.1 Develop Continue to coordinate with First Responders and coordinate to
  implement and maintain medical assistance procedures in the event of a disaster.
  Remove, required per the Building Code:

  •  Policy 6.5 Support County Hazardous Materials Management Plan (adopted by C.C.
  Ordinance 516) objectives and enforcement of current Fire Code regulations regarding
  the storage of hazardous materials.

  Move forward with the following changes:

  •  Policy 1.3 Work with the County to ensure that all fire equipment remains operable and
  adequate to respond to a major disaster.

  •  Policy 1.4 Cooperate with the Los Angeles County Sheriffs Department to ensure that law
  enforcement services are ready and available to serve the City in the event of a major
  disaster.

  Combine policies 1.3 and 1.4 – Cooperate with Los Angeles County Office of Emergency
  Management and utilize county disaster reporting software to monitor and convey
  conditions and operational standards as a result of incident or emergencies or disasters

Move forward with no changes:

  •  Policy 1.5 Support earthquake strengthening and provision of alternative or backup
  services, such as water, sewer, electricity, and natural gas pipelines connections,
  especially in areas of high seismic or geologic high hazard or where weak segments are
  identified by existing or future studies.

Remove:

  •  Policy 2.1 – Discourage development which is adjacent to earthquake faults and other
  geological hazards. Not needed.

  •  Policy 2.5 Continue to require preliminary investigations of tract sites by State-registered
  geotechnical engineers and certified engineering geologists (Chapter 70 County Building
  Code) and ensure regular inspection of grading operations.

Move forward with no changes:

  •  Policy 2.6 Encourage resident to plant groundcover to reduce the brush fire hazard in
  areas adjacent to canyons, and maintain native drought tolerant slope cover and provide
  appropriate irrigation to maintain plant cover and prevent erosion.

Move forward with the following changes:

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  3
 MEETING MINUTES, JANUARY 30, 2020
   •  Policy 2.7 Maintain storm drains drainage systems to prevent local flooding and debris
  flows, and encourage educate residents to assist in maintaining maintain those drains
  drainage systems that are the responsibility of the homeowner.

Remove, a requirement of CEQA compliance:

  •  Policy 2.9 Avoid construction in canyon bottoms and participate in the National Flood
  Insurance Program. Require new development or expansion of existing development
  adjacent to canyons to assess potential environmental impacts from increased run-off and
  erosion and evaluate appropriate mitigation.
Remove, currently being done by CalWater:

  •  Policy 2.11 Support the development of secondary water supplies for emergency water
  flow needs in an emergency.
Move forward with no changes:

  •  Policy 3.2 Inventory and, where necessary, acquire supplemental disaster communication
  equipment and other equipment, tools and supplies.
Move forward with the following changes:

  •  Policy 3.5 Ensure that the City Hall maintains a current emergency supply of water, food,
  blankets and first aid to provide for all its employees for a 3 day period.
Move forward with no changes:

  •  Policy 3.6 Encourage private businesses to develop disaster preparedness plans for their
  employees.
Move forward with the following changes:
    Policy 3.8 Increase public awareness of City emergency response plans, evacuation
  routes and shelters, and in ways to reduce risks at the home and office.
Move forward with no changes:
    Policy 3.10 Coordinate emergency planning efforts with building managers of high-
  occupancy facilities, dependent care centers (nursing homes, day care centers, etc.) and
  critical facilities located in the City to facilitate emergency response.

MBI has agreed to revise the following policies and bring a draft to the next GPAC meeting:
    Policy 4.1 Provide City officials with a basis protocols for disaster preparedness decision
  making and establish a public education program for disaster preparedness.

    Policy 4.2 Establish Maintain a line of command to ensure that the decision making
  process will function satisfactorily in the event of a major disaster.

    Policy 4.4 Encourage cooperation among adjacent communities to provide back-up law
  enforcement assistance in emergency situations.

6.  CONSULTANT/STAFF/COMMITTEE ITEMS

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 7:58 p.m. The next General Plan Advisory Committee
Meeting will be held on Tuesday, March 17, 2020, at 6:00 p.m.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  4
 MEETING MINUTES, JANUARY 30, 2020
